changes.change: post() writes a post one part at a time (a draft/multiline batch, or a line) and confirms each against an absolute per-part deadline before the next; an error reply never counts as confirmation and a refusal outranks channel recreation; each confirmed part records its confirmation time; a failure raises PostIncomplete (or Refused) carrying every part's state (confirmed, uncertain or unsent); parts are fixed on the first write and a retry resends exactly those that are not confirmed, never re-split; queued_entry() keeps only the unconfirmed remainder; outbox_summary(), outbox_flushing() and dead_letter_post() support the bridge and pchat status.
changes.reason: A long post whose completion timed out after the server had committed it was queued whole and reposted on every outbox flush, each copy with new msgids (#19). Deliberate deviation from c572bad, by the owner's authorization on 2026-10-09 to repair this transport defect (issue #19; recorded in docs/plateia_design.md alongside D-70). The running tools keep the baseline behavior until activation (D-23).

changes.change: pchat post queues only the unconfirmed remainder of a post that failed partway and says how many parts were posted; a refusal after some parts were published is recorded in dead letters with its parts; pchat status reports outbox posts awaiting a delivery check and each partly published dead-lettered post's progress.
changes.reason: pchat queued the whole text on any failure, including a completion timeout after the server had committed the post (#19). changes.change: Record._load builds the msgid deduplication set from every line of a channel's log instead of the newest 5,000.
changes.reason: Deliberate deviation from c572bad, by owner decision on PR #16's first review: a catch-up cut short leaves the checkpoint behind, so after a restart more than 5,000 replayed messages would be logged again and an accepted request queued again (PLT-15 requirement 8). The running bridge keeps the baseline behavior until activation.

changes.change: flush_outbox rewrites each claimed file after every change and removes it only when empty, so a crash leaves exactly what is still owed; a part caught mid-write is uncertain and is reconciled against the channel record (delivered, absent only over a record known complete through a sync well after the write, else undecided, dead-lettered with a content-free owner alert after a day) instead of being resent; each part needs its own logged message written no earlier than the part, and a msgid once counted (kept in outbox-attributed.jsonl) is never counted again; a part the server confirmed without our learning its msgid, pending or retired (kept in outbox-reserved.jsonl), keeps a message of its own within its write-to-confirmation window, so one message never satisfies two parts; giving up on an entry is marked durably before it is dead-lettered and retired, so a crash can neither make it retryable nor strand it, and a server refusal is always terminal; announce() queues only the unconfirmed remainder; run() tracks where each channel's record is complete (record-coverage.json) and syncs with a PING before each flush; leaving a channel (KICK or PART) stops its interval until a catch-up after rejoining, and a catch-up still open when it was left completes nothing.
changes.reason: Stop the outbox reposting committed parts of a long post on every flush, and never resend a part that may already be in the channel without proof of absence (#19). Deliberate deviation from c572bad, by the owner's authorization on 2026-10-09 to repair this transport defect (issue #19; recorded in docs/plateia_design.md alongside D-70). The running tools keep the baseline behavior until activation (D-23).
